defect.description: The setting is read as settings['FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE'] or False instead of settings.getbool(...): command-line overrides arrive as text, so -s FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE=False (or =0) gives the non-empty string 'False', which is truthy and turns active mode on.

review_items: feedstorage.py:27 'or False' treats CLI string 'false' as truthy, enabling active mode; use getbool (important)
feedstorage.py:27 'or False' is dead code since key is in DEFAULTS (nit)
test uses native True only; add from_command_line string tests (nit)
no test verifies store() calls set_pasv(False) (nit)
ftp.quit() not in try/finally, connection leak (pre-existing)
votes.evidence_quote: `settings["FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE"] or False` treats the CLI string `"false"` as truthy, enabling active mode when the user explicitly requested it off.
votes.justification: The review names the exact cause at from_settings: a raw CLI string such as 'false' is truthy, so active mode turns on when the user asked for it off. It also gives getbool as the fix, which matches the known defect.
